title: Billing at a kirana shop when the internet drops
summary: Let a shopkeeper keep billing through outages and still end the day with correct stock and accounts.
context: Kadlekai Kart sells a billing app to 25,000 neighbourhood shops. Most run on one Android phone, some on a phone and a tablet. Power cuts and patchy data are ordinary, and a shop cannot turn customers away while the network recovers.
Shop owners read their sales and stock on a second phone at home in the evening. Prices are often changed from there too, so the counter may be billing on a price that has already changed.
must_handle: Billing works with no connection for at least three days.
Two devices in one shop can both sell the last packet while offline.
A bill number must never repeat within a shop, because it goes on a tax record.
A phone that is lost must not lose the unsynced bills without anyone knowing.
An update of the app must not strand data held on an older format.
show_in_answer: What is stored on the device, and what the server treats as the record.
How a day of offline bills reaches the server.
What you do when two devices disagree, case by case.
How a shopkeeper finds out that something did not sync.
